issues.note: British IPA has an unreduced second vowel; it should be ˈpreɡ.nənt.
The time-before-adjective fact appears in three fields, against one fact one field.
Pregnant pause is common; formal fits better than literary, but this is debatable.
Strongly pregnant is not English; the collocation is heavily pregnant.
Predicative 'pregnant with meaning' is common, so 'attributive only' is wrong.
This duplicates the learner error and the adaptation note on the time-before order.
The clause is awkward, but the proposed subject restriction belongs in the explanation.
The same fact is stated three times across fields.
The politeness of expecting is stated in two fields with two wordings.
The usage note restates the learner error on with versus of.

findings.F1: The British IPA has an unreduced second vowel (nænt instead of nənt).
findings.F2: The collocation 'strongly pregnant' is not real; it should be 'heavily pregnant'.
findings.F3: The time-before-pregnant rule is repeated in the explanation, a learner error, and the adaptation note.
findings.F4: Sense 2 is wrongly coded attributive only; predicative 'pregnant with meaning' is common.
findings.F5: The politeness of 'expecting' is stated in both the synonym note and the usage note.
findings.F6: The usage note repeats the 'pregnant with, not of' learner error.
